Real New Haven FQHC that accepts HUSKY and provides pediatric dental services; the receiving dental provider in this use case. Runs a dental PMS with an interim FHIR server. Individual clinicians (Dr. David Watson) are fictional. NPI shown is synthetic, not the real organization's actual NPI.

Real institution — Connie is Connecticut's state-designated statewide HIE (CGS Sec. 17b-59d/e), built as part of the state's Medicaid Enterprise System. In this use case Connie is the central routing hub: it routes the referral to BeneCare, routes the pre-encounter medical records from the Epic FHIR endpoint at Yale New Haven Health to the dental practice, and (at later interactions) routes the encounter summaries back to the medical care team. Named OHIA member organization (sector: State HIE).

Real — the HUSKY / Covered CT dental plan brand, administered by the BeneCare ASO under contract with Connecticut DSS. CTDHP handles the provider network, Plan-Net directory, referral coordination, member services, and prior-authorization / post-procedure review intake — it is NOT the claims payer. Dental claims (837D) are adjudicated and paid by Gainwell (the DSS fiscal agent). There is no dental MCO in the HUSKY model.

Real — the Administrative Services Organization (ASO) that administers CTDHP for Connecticut DSS (selected 2008). BeneCare facilitates administration: Plan-Net provider directory, referral receipt + coordination, prior-authorization / post-procedure review intake, and member services. It is NOT the claims payer and does not adjudicate 837D claims — those are adjudicated and paid by Gainwell (the DSS fiscal agent). The Plan-Net provider directory query in this use case is directed at the CTDHP/BeneCare network directory.

Real — the Connecticut DSS fiscal agent that runs the Medicaid Management Information System / CT Medical Assistance Program (CMAP, ctdssmap.com). Gainwell performs eligibility verification (270/271), DTR and PAS where prior authorization applies, and adjudicates and pays all dental claims (837D in, 835 out). It is the entity that actually administers the HUSKY plan operationally (claims/payment). There is no dental MCO in this model.

payload.contentString: Oral hygiene education: proper brushing technique, daily flossing, and age-appropriate toothpaste guidance for a six-year-old with mixed dentition and elevated periodontal risk from Type 1 diabetes. Toothbrush, toothpaste, and floss dispensed. Reinforced coordination of dental care with diabetes management.

note.text: The oral-hygiene education delivered to Timothy and his grandmother, paired with the D1330 Procedure. Delivered to the accompanying caregiver (grandparent). Not a patient-app notification event.

Confirmed at the dental visit: the plaque-induced gingivitis (K05.00) found at the well-child visit has progressed. Coded as aggressive periodontitis, localized, slight (ICD-10-CM K05.211, verified against the 2026 ICD-10-CM). 'Aggressive' rather than 'chronic' is deliberate and clinically correct: chronic periodontitis is a slow adult disease, whereas the rapid breakdown in a six-year-old with poorly controlled Type 1 diabetes (E10.9) is the aggressive pattern. This Condition is linked to the diabetes as a contributing systemic condition and is transmitted in the Interaction 4 bidirectional summaries.

resource.conclusion: Elevated periodontal risk. Localized slight aggressive periodontitis confirmed in the context of Type 1 diabetes. Scaling and root planing (two quadrants) with localized antimicrobial delivery indicated; reinforce oral hygiene and coordinate with diabetes care team.

resource.description: CQL logic evaluated at order entry for the Connecticut HUSKY B dental benefit (CTDHP): does a D4341 (periodontal scaling and root planing, per quadrant) order require prior authorization? Returns true for D4341 orders under this benefit, since scaling and root planing requires PA. The determination is routed through Connie (statewide HIE) and intake-managed by the BeneCare ASO, while Gainwell (DSS fiscal agent, CMAP) performs the downstream DTR/PAS and adjudicates the resulting claim. Not evaluated at the covered-evaluation referral (Interaction 1); evaluated at the treatment visit (Interaction 3).

resource.name: CTDHPD4341PriorAuthRule
resource.title: CTDHP / HUSKY B — D4341 (Scaling & Root Planing) Requires Prior Authorization
resource.description: Coverage-requirements rule for the Connecticut HUSKY B dental benefit (CTDHP). Fires at order-sign when a dental provider plans periodontal scaling and root planing (CDT D4341). Per the Connecticut administration model, this rule is surfaced/routed through Connie (the statewide HIE) with prior-authorization intake handled by the BeneCare ASO, while DTR/PAS evaluation and claims adjudication are performed by Gainwell Technologies (the DSS fiscal agent running CMAP). There is no dental MCO. This rule is not triggered by the covered-evaluation referral (UC03 Interaction 1); it fires only at the treatment visit (Interaction 3).

detail.description: Daily oral hygiene: brushing technique and flossing as instructed; age-appropriate toothpaste
Six-month periodontal recall to reassess and monitor the partially erupted lower central incisor
Coordinate periodontal management with the diabetes care team (glycemic control affects periodontal outcomes and vice versa)

note.text: Post-treatment care plan surfaced to Timothy's guardian-facing app alongside the visit-complete milestone at Interaction 4. Recall interval and oral-hygiene reinforcement reflect the elevated periodontal risk from Type 1 diabetes.

code.text: Dental encounter summary — to pediatric endocrinologist

assessor.display: Dr. David Watson, DDS — Cornell Scott-Hill Health Center

resource.summary: Timothy Jones, six-year-old male with Type 1 diabetes (E10.9), seen 2026-05-28 for dental evaluation. Aggressive periodontitis (K05.211), localized, slight, confirmed. Periodontal disease progression accelerated by poorly controlled glycemia - this relationship is bidirectional: periodontitis also exacerbates glycemic dysregulation and may complicate insulin management. Scaling and root planing performed (D4341 x2). Chlorhexidine 2.5% chip placed at affected periodontal sites (D4381). Most recent HbA1c requested from chart if available - not available in records received. Recommend glycemic review given periodontal disease burden in the context of ongoing diabetes management.

note.text: Structured summary to the pediatric endocrinologist (Yale Children's Diabetes Program) via Connie — the second of the two simultaneous Interaction 4 summaries. Its clinical point is the bidirectional oral-systemic relationship: it carries the NEW periodontal->glycemic risk Flag (flag-perio-glycemic-risk), which points in the OPPOSITE direction from the Interaction 1 diabetes->periodontal Flag. The two Flags must not be conflated.

code.text: Dental encounter summary — to referring pediatrician

assessor.display: Dr. David Watson, DDS — Cornell Scott-Hill Health Center

resource.summary: Timothy Jones seen 2026-05-28 per referral from Northeast Medical Group. Comprehensive oral evaluation and periodontal risk assessment completed. Gingivitis has progressed to early-stage aggressive periodontitis (K05.211), localized, slight - consistent with the accelerated periodontitis trajectory in Type 1 diabetes. Scaling and root planing performed in two quadrants (D4341 x2). Chlorhexidine chip placed at affected sites (D4381). Oral hygiene education provided to patient and grandmother (D1330); toothbrush, toothpaste, and floss dispensed. Six-month recall recommended. Permanent restoration of partially erupted lower central incisor to be monitored at recall.

note.text: Structured encounter summary returned to the referring pediatrician (Dr. Smith, NEMG) via Connie — one of two simultaneous summaries at Interaction 4 (the other goes to the endocrinologist). This summary closes the referral loop (see the completed referral Task and ServiceRequest). Transmitted as discrete FHIR, not a PDF.

code.text: Active periodontal disease (aggressive periodontitis) — may exacerbate glycemic dysregulation and complicate insulin management. Recommend glycemic review and coordinated care.

note.text: NEW Flag raised at Interaction 4, directed to the pediatric endocrinologist. This is the periodontal->glycemic-risk direction (periodontitis worsening glycemic control), the OPPOSITE of the Interaction 1 Flag (flag-diabetes-perio-risk), which was the diabetes->periodontal-risk direction directed to the dental provider. Two distinct Flags pointed in opposite directions — deliberately not the same Flag reused. Travels with the endocrinologist summary (clinicalimpression-summary-endocrinologist).
